theme: Letting one molecule through and not its twin
title: Letting One Molecule Through and Not Its Twin: Membrane Selectivity Design
strategies: echo the wide-open, chemistry-free membrane -- reproduces the checker's own baseline construction (Ratio ~0.1)

pure size-sieving: binary-search the smallest single pore radius that still clears the throughput requirement, alpha always 0 -- works reasonably when target and twin differ noticeably in size, but on near-identical-twin cases collapses to the baseline because no radius separates them and no alpha=0 design can even reach the required throughput there

joint pore-distribution + chemistry optimization: blend a highly-selective small radius with a wide-open radius to trade permeability against selectivity, AND dial up the functionalization loading alpha to exploit the target/twin affinity gap (the solubility channel) -- an orthogonal trade-off curve that stays effective even when the size channel is blind
gradient-free joint search over (alpha, pore-blend) with finer resolution, or exact per-alpha optimization of the two-point blend weight
